questions.stem: The Retail Exchange Company has all of their applications in a single system of record and ownership has been established. Which level of the maturity model are they in right now?
questions.explanation: The APM maturity model has 4 levels. Level 1 (Applications Under Management) means all applications are in a single system of record with ownership established. Level 2 (Basic Rationalization) involves initial scoring and assessment. Level 3 (Advanced Rationalization) adds strategic planning. Level 4 (Continuously Optimized Portfolio) represents ongoing optimization. Since the company has a single system of record with established ownership but hasn't started rationalization yet, they're at Level 1.

questions.stem: What does the Load Application Indicators and Compute Application Scores job do?

options.text: Generates scores for all indicators and business applications across selected profiles
Generates scores for selected indicators and selected applications across all profiles
Generates scores for all indicators and business applications across all profiles
Generates scores for all indicators and selected applications across all profiles

questions.explanation: The 'Load Application Indicators and Compute Application Scores' scheduled job recalculates scores for ALL indicators, ALL scoring profiles those indicators are attached to, and ALL business applications associated with those profiles. It generates scores based on the frequency set on each indicator (monthly, quarterly, yearly). The job is comprehensive — it doesn't filter by specific indicators or applications. Answer C correctly describes this all-encompassing scope.

questions.stem: APM combines with several ServiceNow technologies to provide a comprehensive view of your customer’s application portfolio. Why would a customer want to utilize information from ServiceNow ServiceMapping? (Choose two.)

options.text: Identify your customer’s applications’ underlying technologies.
Produce a horizontal picture of a customer’s business applications.

questions.explanation: Service Mapping discovers and maps application services and their underlying infrastructure relationships. For APM, this provides two key benefits: (A) identifying underlying technologies that applications depend on (servers, databases, middleware), and (B) identifying application services themselves by mapping entry points through infrastructure dependencies. Option C ('horizontal picture') describes capability mapping, not Service Mapping. Option D ('application inventory') is a Discovery/CMDB function, not specific to Service Mapping's value to APM.

questions.stem: What are the 4 sections of the APM portal home page that is aligned to The Open Group Architecture Framework (TOGAF)? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: The APM portal home page aligns with TOGAF (The Open Group Architecture Framework) which defines four architecture domains: Business, Application, Data/Information, and Technology. The corresponding APM sections are: (A) Information Portfolio, (D) Application Portfolio, (E) Business Portfolio, and (F) Technology Portfolio. Service Portfolio (B) and Catalog Portfolio (C) are not part of TOGAF's architecture domains. TOGAF's four domains map directly to these four APM portal sections.

questions.stem:
APM interfaces with Software Asset Management to pull this application data:
(Choose three.)
questions.explanation: APM integrates with Software Asset Management (SAM) to pull three types of application data: (A) Product Classification — how software is classified/categorized, (B) Software Model Data — details about the software product including publisher and version, and (D) Lifecycle Data — end-of-life and support dates for software products. Hardware Asset Lifecycle (C) comes from HAM, not SAM. Vendor Procurement (E) is a procurement function, not a SAM data point pulled into APM.

questions.stem: Which attributes can be used to categorize business applications? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: Business applications can be categorized using these attributes: (C) Application Family — groups related apps together, (D) Portfolio — assigns apps to a portfolio for management, (E) Category — functional classification of the app, and (F) Business Unit — organizational grouping. Application Score (A) is a calculated metric, not a categorization attribute. Application Name (B) is an identifier, not a way to categorize. The four categorization attributes help organize and filter the application inventory by different dimensions.

questions.stem: The capability map provides a hierarchical view of the business capabilities in an organization. How many levels does the capability hierarchy support in its series?
questions.explanation: The business capability map in APM supports a hierarchy of up to 6 levels in its series. The hierarchy starts at level 0 (root capabilities) and can go down to level 5, for a total of 6 levels. This allows organizations to model business capabilities from broad strategic functions down to specific operational activities. The capability map uses a tree structure where each capability can have child capabilities within these 6 levels.

questions.stem: Why would enterprise architects be interested in APM outcomes? (Choose two.)

options.text: Understand what software licenses need to be reclaimed
Understand the landscape of technology standards and lifecycle plans
View business capabilities supported by applications

questions.explanation: Enterprise architects use APM for strategic technology planning, not operational IT tasks. (C) Understanding the landscape of technology standards and lifecycle plans helps architects identify technology risks, plan migrations, and set standards. (D) Viewing business capabilities supported by applications enables gap analysis and rationalization decisions. Incident counts (A) are operational metrics for IT operations, not architectural planning. Software license reclamation (B) is a SAM/asset management concern, not an enterprise architecture outcome.

questions.stem: What relationship type is used to describe a relationship between a business capability and a business application?
questions.explanation: The relationship between a business capability and a business application uses 'Provides::Provided by'. From the application's perspective, it 'Provides' one or more business capabilities. From the capability's perspective, it is 'Provided by' one or more applications. 'Used by/Uses' (A) describes a different dependency type. 'Depends on/Used by' (B) is for technical dependencies. 'Runs on/Runs' (D) describes hosting relationships (e.g., app runs on server), not functional capability relationships.

questions.stem: When a business application request is approved, a record is created in the business application table. What is the state of the business application at this point?
questions.explanation: When a business application request is approved in APM, a record is created in the business application table [cmdb_ci_business_app] with the state set to 'Implementing'. This reflects that the application has been approved but is not yet in production — it's being set up, configured, or deployed. The lifecycle then progresses through states like Pilot, In Production, and eventually Retired. It wouldn't immediately be 'In Production' (C) since approval precedes deployment.

questions.stem: Which of the following fields represents the granular licensable version of the software and is used to calculate the technology risk?
questions.explanation: The Lifecycle Full Version field represents the most granular licensable version of software (e.g., 'Windows Server 2019 Standard 10.0.17763') and is used to calculate technology risk. Technology risk assessment compares this detailed version against known end-of-life dates. Lifecycle Model (A) is the broader product line (e.g., 'Windows Server'). Lifecycle Release (C) is the major release (e.g., '2019'). 'Ignore Technical Risk' (B) is a boolean flag to exclude an app from risk calculation, not a version field.

questions.stem: What is the guiding framework that a project team should use when designing the APM architecture?
questions.explanation: The Common Service Data Model (CSDM) is the guiding framework for designing APM architecture. CSDM provides a standardized data model that defines how business services, application services, and technical services relate to each other and to the underlying infrastructure. ITIL (A) is a broader IT service management framework, not specific to application architecture. PMP (B) is a project management methodology. DIO (D) is not a recognized ServiceNow framework.

questions.stem: What key components of ServiceNow does APM leverage? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: APM leverages three key ServiceNow components: (A) Discovery identifies hardware and software CIs in the environment, building the foundational inventory. (B) Service Mapping maps application services to their underlying infrastructure dependencies. (D) Application Services represent the logical grouping of CIs that deliver a service. Service Catalog (C) is for request fulfillment and HR (E) is a separate product — neither is a core APM dependency.

questions.stem: Stephen discovers that his customer is looking to achieve Basic Rationalization including application scoring. What APM maturity level does this align to?
questions.explanation: The APM maturity model has 4 levels: Level 1 (Applications Under Management) — single system of record with ownership. Level 2 (Basic Rationalization) — initial application scoring and assessment. Level 3 (Advanced Rationalization) — strategic planning with roadmaps. Level 4 (Continuously Optimized Portfolio) — ongoing optimization. Since Stephen's customer wants basic rationalization including application scoring, this aligns to Level 2.

questions.stem: When you approve a retire a Business Application request, which system property determines whether a project or a demand is created?
questions.explanation: The system property sn_apm.retireBusinessApplicationTaskType determines whether approving a 'Retire a Business Application' request creates a project or a demand record. This property lets administrators control the workflow — setting it to 'project' creates a project task to track the retirement, while 'demand' creates a demand record for evaluation. The other options are not valid APM system property names.

questions.stem: What are the three segments of the Business Application Costing Model? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: The Business Application Costing Model, enabled by the Financial Management for APM plugin, breaks down application costs into three segments: (A) Business Processes — costs associated with business processes the app supports, (C) Business Applications — direct costs of maintaining and licensing the application itself, and (D) IT Shared Services — infrastructure and shared service costs allocated to the app. Manufacturers (B) and Business Units (E) are not cost model segments.

questions.stem: What is the name of the basic plugin for the APM application?
questions.explanation: The basic plugin for APM is 'Application Portfolio Management' (com.snc.apm), now called Enterprise Architecture. The Activate docs state: 'The Enterprise Architecture (com.snc.apm) plugin is the basic plugin for the application.' Business Planner (B) is a related plugin activated by it. Financial Management for APM (C) is an optional add-on. ATF Tests (D) is for automated testing validation, not the base plugin.

questions.stem: What are the business problems that customers are trying to resolve by utilizing Application Portfolio Management (APM)? (Choose two.)

options.text: Gain a comprehensive understanding of business applications in the organization
Reduce the number of governance controls
Identify redundancies and decrease budgetary costs

questions.explanation: APM helps customers resolve two key business problems: (A) gaining a comprehensive understanding of business applications in the organization, and (C) identifying redundancies and decreasing budgetary costs. APM provides visibility into the entire application portfolio, enabling rationalization to eliminate duplicate applications and reduce spending. Governance controls (B) and vendor relationships (D) are not core APM objectives.

questions.stem: Stephen is attempting to summarize for the customer how all of the applications that support APM are brought together. From the bottom-up, what ServiceNow application supports the first layer of CI Iinventory?
questions.explanation: In the APM application stack, Discovery forms the foundational bottom layer. It scans the network to identify and populate CI inventory — hardware, software, and their relationships. From bottom-up: Discovery provides the CI inventory base, SAM adds software model and lifecycle data, Service Mapping links CIs into application services, and APM sits on top for portfolio analysis. Since the question asks about the first layer of CI inventory, Discovery (A) is the correct answer.

questions.stem: If a customer asks you how ServiceNow’s ServiceMapping application works in order to support APM, how would you explain it?

options.text: Identifies all hardware and software CI’s and other dependencies that support that service.
Drills down to provide application services, vulnerabilities and risks.
Creates an API to manage seamless application services.
Provides software entitlements through a top-down approach.

questions.explanation: Service Mapping works by identifying all hardware and software CIs and other dependencies that support a given application service. It starts from an entry point (URL, port, etc.) and maps outward, discovering all the underlying infrastructure components — servers, databases, load balancers, middleware — that the service depends on. This top-down approach creates a complete dependency map. Option B describes vulnerability scanning, C describes an API gateway, and D describes SAM's approach.

questions.stem: What is the value of managing applications using ServiceNow?

options.text: Allows data collection and visualization without manual effort
Provides application owners insight to release counts
Provides top down strategic alignment in the PMO

questions.explanation: The primary value of managing applications using ServiceNow APM is that it allows data collection and visualization without manual effort. APM integrates with Discovery, Service Mapping, and other data sources to automatically gather application data, then visualizes it through dashboards, bubble charts, and scorecards. This automation eliminates the need for manual spreadsheet tracking that most organizations rely on.

questions.stem: What is the overall score range that a business application could have?
questions.explanation: Business applications in APM have an overall score range of 1 through 100. The score is calculated by the scoring job that processes all indicators and profiles, aggregating them into a composite score. This 1-100 range provides granular differentiation between applications for rationalization and portfolio analysis purposes.

questions.stem: Which portal is the best data source to capture strategies, goals and capabilities?
questions.explanation: The Business Planning Portal is the best data source to capture strategies, goals, and capabilities. This portal provides a structured interface for enterprise architects and business stakeholders to define organizational strategy, map business capabilities, and align goals. The APM Portal focuses on application health, while the Application Navigator is just the SN navigation menu.

questions.stem: Which job will generate scores for all indicators and business applications across all profiles?

options.text: Load Application Indicators and Compute Application Scores
Analyze PA scores and PA snapshot tables
Load TPM Risk Parameters and compute Application Service Risks

questions.explanation: The 'Load Application Indicators and Compute Application Scores' scheduled job generates scores for all indicators and business applications across all profiles. This job runs the indicator sourcing and score calculation process, evaluating every indicator for every application against all defined profiles to produce the composite application scores used in APM dashboards and bubble charts.

questions.stem: What are the stages of the APM rationalization process?

options.text: Measure, Evaluate, Decide, Take Action, Baseline
Identify, Measure, Evaluate, Decide, Take Action
Identify, Measure, Decide, Take Action, Communicate
Identify, Measure, Evaluate, Take Action, Certify

questions.explanation: The APM rationalization process follows five stages: Identify (discover and catalog all applications), Measure (score applications using indicators), Evaluate (analyze scores against business value and technical fitness), Decide (determine the strategy — invest, tolerate, migrate, or eliminate), and Take Action (execute the strategy via projects/demands). Option B correctly lists all five stages in order. The other options either include incorrect stages or are in wrong order.

questions.stem: What application metrics does APM provide to a manager in order for him or her to make targeted decisions based on data instead of educated guesses? (Choose two.)

options.text: Costs it takes to maintain an application.
One or more use rights assigned to a specific device or user.
Compliance to regulations and organizational standards.

questions.explanation: APM provides application metrics to help managers make data-driven decisions. The two relevant metrics are: (A) Costs to maintain an application — financial indicators showing total cost of ownership, licensing, and operational costs. (C) Compliance to regulations and organizational standards — risk and compliance indicators measuring adherence to standards. Option B (use rights assigned to device/user) describes SAM license entitlements. Option D (application's age) alone isn't a standard APM metric.

questions.stem: What customer stakeholder group would be interested in knowing the business value and health of applications?
questions.explanation: Enterprise Architects are the stakeholder group most interested in knowing the business value and health of applications. They are responsible for application portfolio strategy, technology roadmaps, and rationalization decisions. APM's bubble charts, scorecards, and health dashboards are primarily designed for EA consumption to make informed decisions about application investment, retirement, and consolidation.

questions.stem: What links the application service to the underlying technologies?
questions.explanation: The Application Service Software Model links the application service to the underlying technologies. A software model in ServiceNow represents the canonical definition of a software product (publisher, version, lifecycle). When an application service is associated with a software model, it creates the connection between the logical service and the actual technology components it runs on. Application Management Model (A), Inventory Management (B), and Application Category (D) don't serve this linking function.

questions.stem: What information does Hardware Asset Management provide to support decisions about business applications and application services?
questions.explanation: Hardware Asset Management (HAM) provides Hardware Lifecycle data to support decisions about business applications. HAM tracks the lifecycle stages of physical hardware — procurement, deployment, end-of-life, and disposal dates. When hardware supporting an application approaches end-of-life, this creates technology risk that impacts application planning decisions. Software Lifecycle (A) comes from SAM, not HAM. Business Capability (B) and Application Capability (C) are APM concepts, not HAM data.

questions.stem: During the customer workshop, Kelly was identified as needing a role that would grant access to create bubble charts, set-up application classification attributes and assessment indicators. Which role should be assigned to Kelly?
questions.explanation: The sn_apm.apm_admin role grants access to create bubble charts, set up application classification attributes, and assessment indicators. The admin docs state: 'With the sn_apm.apm_admin role, you can classify the applications... set up application classification attributes... assessment indicators, and create bubble charts.' The apm_analyst (C) can create application records and access dashboards but lacks the admin-level configuration ability. apm_user (B) only views/updates apps. business_planner (D) is for the Business Planning portal.

questions.stem: What type of notifications are displayed on the Application Portfolio Management Portal?

options.text: Project tasks that are due on the current date or the next week.
Monthly listing of current demands submitted by application.
Incident alerts per application for the current day and unresolved incidents.
The number of software models that have high risks expiring on the current date or the next 90 days.
